use default

class CUTTER is
    width: int
    height: int
    last: int
    grid: LIST[int]
    steps: int[]
    moves: (int, int)[]
    count: long

    init(height: int, width: int) is
        self.height = height
        self.width = width
        last = (height + 1) * (width + 1) - 1
        grid = repeat(0, last + 1) |> collect_list()
        steps = [-1, -width - 1, 1, width + 1]
        moves = [(0, -1), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0)]
        count = 0L
    si

    walk(y: int, x: int) is
        if y == 0 \/ y == height \/ x == 0 \/ x == width then
            count = count + 2L
            return
        fi

        let t = y * (width + 1) + x

        grid[t] = grid[t] + 1
        grid[last - t] = grid[last - t] + 1

        for (i, (dy, dx)) in moves |> index() do
            if grid[t + steps[i]] == 0 then
                walk(y + dy, x + dx)
            fi
        od

        grid[t] = grid[t] - 1
        grid[last - t] = grid[last - t] - 1
    si

    from_centre() -> long is
        let middle_y = height / 2, middle_x = width / 2

        for x in middle_x + 1..width do
            let t = middle_y * (width + 1) + x

            grid[t] = 1
            grid[last - t] = 1
            walk(middle_y - 1, x)
        od

        count + 1L
    si
si

cuts(h: int, w: int) -> long is
    let (tall, wide) = if h % 2 == 1 then (w, h) else (h, w) fi

    if tall % 2 == 1 then
        return 0L
    fi

    if wide == 1 then return 1L fi
    if wide == 2 then return cast long(tall) fi
    if tall == 2 then return cast long(wide) fi

    let ways = CUTTER(tall, wide).from_centre()

    if tall == wide then
        return 2L * ways
    fi

    if wide % 2 == 0 then
        return ways + CUTTER(wide, tall).from_centre() - 1L
    fi

    ways
si

for h in 1::9 do
    for w in 1::h do
        if h % 2 == 0 \/ w % 2 == 0 then
            write_line("{h} x {w}: {cuts(h, w)}")
        fi
    od
od
